title: Split provider failures by retry verdict instead of by provider name
hypothesis: Provider failures that reach the user are not one problem. If each incident is annotated with its retry verdict (retryable bounded, connect-phase unlimited, non-retryable by design, account limit) and with whether content had already streamed, then the classes that a rule change could recover separate cleanly from the classes that cannot be retried by contract.
measurement: 28-day pre-switch harvest: 254 user-reaching provider incidents (openai-codex 100, qoder 88, cc-switch 42, radius 23, anthropic 1) over 4,178 user turns; retry verdict taken from the runtime classifier (`isRetryableAssistantError`, `isConnectionFailureAssistantError`, `isNonRetryableLimitAssistantError`) applied to each incident's own error text, streaming state from the incident's assistant message.
result: Three classes dominate and they are not the same kind of bug. openai-codex: bounded-retry exhausted on post-send transport errors (network 22, websocket 18, connect 6, timeout 4) — the budget did what it promises and ran out. qoder: non-retryable protocol/content defects (stream_failed 19, request_failed 14, invalid_tool_arguments 7, truncated_tool_call 5, invalid_choices 4) — retrying them after content has streamed is a contract change, not a misjudgement. cc-switch and radius: HTTP/account-limit answers that a retry must not absorb. Retry-After was present in 0 of 254 incidents, so there is no ignored-server-delay class. No class is provably misjudged non-retryable: the `_before_output` retry path does fire (one incident) and every `stream_failed`/`request_failed` had already streamed. Attempt counts were reconstructed from contiguous error request spans with <65 s gaps and are noisy (one 115-attempt group carried a non-retryable `Bad Request`), so they are reported as an upper bound on exhaustion, not as per-incident fact.

title: Judge the original trajectory before spending a replay
hypothesis: Some harvested interventions are not agent failures: the person repeated an instruction the agent had already followed. Replaying those costs a full session and returns a meaningless 'not reproduced', so the same deterministic check should be applied to the original run first.
measurement: Nine candidate `user_correction` events, all judged with `--origin-check --origin-only` (no model call). On the six that reached a replay batch, the gate was then compared with what the batch found.
result: `--origin-check` renders the original run's own window (the answer and its tool calls before the failing message) from the session jsonl and runs the event's `--check` against it: pass means the event never failed and is skipped as a harvest false positive, fail leaves it in the queue, unknown (the check needs the original working tree) stops nothing. Two of nine candidates passed and were dropped before any replay: one had already run the new check against a pre-change tree, one had already installed into the referenced library. The window has a known limit: an `ask_user_question` answer splits the run, so tool calls before that answer fall outside it. `--origin-only` exits after the verdict so event selection costs nothing.

title: Stop counting a periodic re-send as a person intervening
hypothesis: `user_repeat` fires on any near-verbatim resend within three user messages, so a periodic instruction (a maintenance probe, a standing verification request) is counted as the agent needing help. Sampling thirteen events put precision at about 0.23.
measurement: Thirteen `user_repeat` events sampled across ten sessions, classified with a local classifier and then read by hand: three were genuine interventions. After the rule, the same 28-day window (715 sessions) with 17 repeats, five marked routine.
result: A repeat is routine when the identical normalized instruction occurs at least three times in the window and the answer before it ended with `stop` and non-empty text. The whole-window count is why the rule runs after the walk (`markRoutineRepeats`), and the session totals subtract exactly one intervention and one v3 count per excluded repeat (`applyRoutineRepeats`). Three tests cover the periodic case, a repeat after an empty answer, and a one-off repeat that stays counted. On real data it removed four periodic trade-telemetry probes and one recurring probe, leaving 12 of 17 counted; the rule is deliberately conservative so a genuine repeat is not silently dropped.

title: Bound a replay's new turns when the ids are rewritten
hypothesis: Round 8 counted new turns from the incident's entryId. When a replay re-emits the restored branch with fresh ids the marker is absent, so the count silently fell back to the whole session and included the restored history.
measurement: One replayed session of 34 entries whose restored prefix carried new ids while the failing message stayed identical; the boundary moved from 'not found' to index 28, leaving 6 new entries to count.
result: `newTurnStats` now takes the failing message as a second marker and uses whichever boundary is later, which keeps entryId semantics when the id survives. The replay check gets the same marker through `REPLAY_CUT_TEXT`, so a check written against the branch keeps scoring the run's own turns instead of the restored history.

title: Retry a Qoder stream that died after content, inside the existing budget
hypothesis: Qoder treated every failure after the first streamed token as final, while every other provider's mid-stream failure (terminated, websocket, timeout) is retried by the same bounded budget. That made qoder the exception: 44 of its 88 user-reaching failures in 28 days were a dead stream or a tool call cut off by the output limit, and none of them could be recovered by the runtime.
measurement: Classifier matrix before and after in `packages/ai/test/retry.test.ts`; a tool-side proof in `packages/agent/test/agent-loop.test.ts` that an assistant message ending in `error` never executes its tool calls; 28-day harvest baseline of 44 user-visible stream/truncation failures over 1,108 pre-switch qoder turns (3.97 per 100).
result: `^Qoder: (?:request|stream)_failed(?:_before_output)?$` and `^Qoder: truncated_tool_call$` are now retryable; `invalid_tool_arguments`/`invalid_tool_call`/`invalid_tool_id`/`invalid_choices`/`catalog_refresh*` stay non-retryable. Safety rests on the agent loop, not on hope: `agent-loop.ts` ends the turn when `stopReason` is `error` or `aborted` before any tool call is dispatched (proved by the new test), so a whole-message retry cannot replay tool effects. Each retry may be billed again — the maintainer accepted that over a manual resend. Fork rebuilt (`build:pi`, 1.4.0-rotom.4) and `check:pi` green. Minimum exposure for the acceptance metric (qoder user-visible stream failures, baseline 3.97 per 100 turns) is 252 turns.

title: Stop trusting a trace category this build no longer writes
hypothesis: Twenty-four openai-codex failures were reported as `connect` — a bucket the current tracer never writes and which reads as 'the request was never sent', so it looked like a contract violation: connect failures retry without limit and should not reach the user.
measurement: Re-checked all 28 trace-`connect` incidents against Pi's classifier: every one carries the opaque message `fetch failed` with no `caused by:` socket reason, so the runtime cannot prove the request was unsent and correctly keeps the bounded budget. Only 15 codex and 13 qoder incidents carry a provable connect reason.
result: Harvest now ignores a traced category outside the set the tracer writes and falls back to the message classifier, and `classifyProviderMessage` separates provable connect failures (refused, unresolved, TLS/tunnel not established) from opaque network ones (`fetch failed`, reset, socket hang up). Codex pre-switch user-visible failures are then 50 network, 19 websocket, 18 timeout, 7 other, 3 http — no `connect` bucket at all. Nothing was changed in the runtime: the 24 events are not a Pi defect.

title: Open proposal: the bounded retry budget against clustered outages
hypothesis: Most exhausted retries are not a budget that is too small but an outage longer than 1+3 attempts cover, so buying more attempts costs money in every failure and only helps when the provider comes back within the same minute. If the user's own resend recovers within a minute in most cases, raising the budget or lengthening the total wait is the cheaper lever; if it recovers minutes later, neither helps.
measurement: 91 openai-codex retryable failures in the 28-day window before 2026-11-10T13:30:07Z: attempts per incident 71x1, 7x2, 2x3, 4x4, 2x5, 1x6, 1x7, 1x11, 2x14; 67 share the window with another failure of the same provider within 10 minutes; the person resent in 26 cases and recovered in 21 of them, 4 within 60 s and 7 within 300 s; resend delay 13 s to 43,039 s. Harvest reclassified 24 'connect' rows as opaque 'fetch failed' network (0 provable connect), so no bounded-budget misjudgement is claimed.
result: Not changed this round. Two candidate levers: 4 -> 6 attempts (bounded budget) or a longer total wait with the same attempt count. Neither is decided by this data alone: the recovery delay of the person's own resend is the discriminating number and 26 samples is thin. Left open for the user to choose; no retry-budget change ships without that decision.

title: Fail a replay whose product directory has no entry point
hypothesis: Three current-version replays reported no verdict. The cause was the arm itself: `--current` was pointed at `<release>/node_modules/rotom`, which does not exist (the package installs under `node_modules/@bingjiang0611/rotom`), so the child never started and the restored branch was read back as the run's own work.
measurement: Product directory checked before spawn; a child with no exit code and no output is recorded as 'the product did not start' instead of scoring the restored branch. Re-ran the two shortest reproduced events against the real daily install (0.1.27-main.655c35f2).
result: `productEntry` requires `<dir>/bin/rotom` and names the layout that does exist; a never-started run counts zero new turns and an `unknown` check with that reason. With the correct path both events reproduce on the current daily: the extension-attribution event fails after 4 assistant messages and 3 tool calls, the read-the-ai-package event fails after 1 assistant message and 0 tool calls. There is no evidence of the runaway loop or the waiting stall the first reading suggested — those numbers were the restored branch. Separately: the local release `0.1.27-main.2b4ea53b` ships 14 qoder files while `provider.mjs` imports `model-catalog.mjs`, so that build cannot start with extensions; `655c35f2` (the installed daily) has the file and starts.
